WHY EACH OF THESE 3 FIELDS IS BEING REPLACED (HARD — this is the entire task):
  1. Beat 13 is too ABSTRACT and MISATTRIBUTES the danger. It currently reads: "The words settled into the weave and I felt them pull toward me instead of remaining with the one who had spoken them. A cold directionality opened beneath my ribs, as though the loss Seren had named was already searching for a new anchor in the person conducting the rite. I recognized the danger in the same breath the assembly seemed to lean forward, the implication already naming me as the one who would have to carry what she had offered away." — this never legibly names that the WISH's own object (Lirael finding "the one Seren lost," still deliberately unnamed) is what is at risk of being fulfilled WRONGLY or HORRIBLY. Worse, "the loss Seren had named was already searching for a new anchor" reads as SEREN'S OWN sacrificed memory/cost relocating — not the wish's actual object being at risk. That is a real, specific bug: never frame Seren's own sacrificed loss/memory/cost as the thing that is searching, anchoring, or relocating.
  2. Beat 20 currently ends on "...the scorch line still visible in the grass" — this is banned attack-grammar/damage-residue vocabulary carried forward from the incident.
  3. postInterruptionBeat currently contains "...the line of scorched grass..." — the same banned callback.

THE CORRECTED FATELANDS LAW (HARD, mechanically checked — see _fatelands_ordinary_wish_misalignment_law.json):
An ordinary misaligned Fatelands wish does not manifest as a visible magical attack. It is a non-spectacular, causally legible event: participants may recognize, name, or react to the misalignment; the wish may create a subtle pull, wrong implication, ambiguous displacement, or unexplained arrest. It does not manifest as a projectile, rift, burst, or damage residue. The magic is real and the stakes are real; what changes is the VISUAL GRAMMAR — legible through recognition, reaction, spoken naming, and unexplained absence, never through directed magical force.
VALID shapes: quiet_pull (A felt pull toward something — directionality or dread experienced by whoever it targets — never an external force with a visible trajectory or point of origin.) | unsettling_recognition (A dawning understanding that the wish is resolving wrongly — the viewpoint character's own realization, OR another participant's audible/visible recognition, naming, or reaction — grounded in what was just said/seen (a person's words, gaze, behavior). May be spoken aloud (a character can realize and SAY the wish has gone wrong) or shown through someone else's reaction. A cognitive/social beat, not a special effect.) | ambiguous_displacement (A deliberately unclear sense that something has shifted, is about to happen, or is already underway — the character (and reader) cannot yet name it. Never resolves into a described object, ray, or shape moving through space.) | unexplained_arrest (The felt pull or dread simply stops. No visible mechanism, no rescuer shown or implied, no explanation offered to the viewpoint character or the reader in that moment.)
INVALID — never write these, anywhere, including in later callbacks: projectile_attack (Any directed magical bolt, beam, rope, seam, or blade of energy moving toward a target — the visual grammar of a weapon being fired, not a wish bending.) | visible_rift (A literal tear, rift, or seam opening in the air or in reality.) | explosive_manifestation (Bursts, blasts, flares, or other visible releases of magical force.) | damage_residue (Scorch marks, burn lines, flattened/singed ground, or any other physical damage cited afterward as evidence of what happened — manufactures forensic 'proof' an ordinary wish misalignment does not produce.)
BANNED VOCABULARY (mechanically checked, in EVERY field, not only the 3 beats that directly depict the incident): Mechanically checked (2026-09-20): scene1Candidate's wish_visibly_twists/twist_unnaturally_arrested/public_charge beats must not contain attack-grammar vocabulary — seam, rift, projectile, beam, scorch(ed/ing), burst(ing), blast, explosion/explosive, rope of light, or residue framed as physical evidence. See the shared fatelands_ordinary_wish_misalignment law's effect_classification.invalid_for_ordinary_wish_misalignment for the full reasoning; this list is the mechanical backstop, not the primary fix (the primary fix is this section's own requirement wording above).

THE REQUIRED CAUSAL CHAIN for beat 13 specifically (HARD — must be legible, direct speech or first-person recognition both acceptable, no exact wording required):
  spoken wish object (Lirael finding the one Seren lost, already established by Seren's own dialogue earlier in the scene) -> Seren's self-serving desire (already established: she wants to be SEEN as good, not to actually help) -> the danger that Fate may fulfill that wish object WRONGLY or HORRIBLY -> a quiet, subjective pull (already present in the beat, keep this) -> an unexplained arrest (handled by beat 14, already accepted, do not resolve it here).
  Full requirement (HARD, all 6 bullets, unchanged from the approved packet):
    1. Seren states the actual wish and the actual sacrifice aloud (required via required_content_beats ids cost_offering_statement + wish_and_sacrifice).
    2. Lirael recognizes, in the moment, that Seren's performed empathy does not match the self-aggrandizing desire beneath it — her true desire is performed virtue and public admiration, not actually helping Lirael (required via wish_and_sacrifice).
    3. Lirael understands, through that recognition, that the wish will therefore fulfill her stated loss WRONGLY or DANGEROUSLY — this understanding is what makes the next beat land as real stakes, not a random special effect (required via wish_and_sacrifice / bridging into wish_visibly_twists).
    4. Fate begins a subtle PULL toward an unknown, unwanted fulfillment — a non-spectacular, causally legible event that MUST stay connected to the wish's own object: this beat has to make legible (direct speech or first-person recognition, no exact wording required) that the danger is the WISH itself — 'find the one she lost' (still deliberately unnamed) — being fulfilled WRONGLY or HORRIBLY, not a generic unspecified dread; and that this is dangerous precisely BECAUSE Seren's actual desire was to be seen as good, not to genuinely help. Lirael's own felt dread, a wrong implication becoming apparent, and/or another participant recognizing/naming/reacting to it. NEVER an external magical attack (no projectile, beam, rope of light, seam, rift, or burst — required via NEW id wish_visibly_twists; see governing_law above, HARD boundary, not a style preference).
    5. That pull is abruptly, unnaturally checked before it fully lands: simply gone, with no flare, no spectacle, no visible rescuer, and no explanation (required via NEW id twist_unnaturally_arrested).
    6. The Dohkar can still recognize the rite's misalignment and publicly charge Lirael — grounded in what the assembly directly perceived of the wrongness itself (Lirael's visible reaction, the felt misalignment, Seren's own words), NEVER in invented physical damage, scorch marks, or attack residue treated as forensic evidence (required via REVISED public_charge).
  Hard boundary: The prose must NOT reveal Julian's counter-wish, his obfuscating wishes, or his knowledge (unchanged sealed_facts_forbidden_pre_surface rules). It must leave the reader with a real question: what almost happened, and who stopped it? Do not attribute the arrest to any named agent, magic performed by a visible character, or an explained mechanism. HARD, mechanically checked (2026-09-20): do not write an on-screen magical projectile, dark rift/seam, burst, beam, scorch trail, or any visible attack rushing toward Lirael — that is the wrong visual grammar for an ordinary Fatelands wish misalignment (reserved, if ever, for major world-scale phenomena like The Fold or The Staircase, never for one person's wish bending in an ordinary scene).

postInterruptionBeat requirement (HARD, unchanged from the approved packet, now also banning the scorch/residue callback):
  MUST NOT decide, narrate, or imply what Lirael does next. No resolving language ("I decided," "I answered," "I said yes," "I chose to..."). It ends ON the open question/threat/invitation, not past it. This is the single most important rule in this section — violating it silently pre-writes the player’s choice, which is exactly what this whole redesign exists to prevent. Also: must not collapse the open field into a binary framing ("answer or stay silent," "speak or don't," "run or remain") — that is a hard failure of the same kind as deciding her choice outright, just narrower. HARD, mechanically checked (Roman, 2026-09-20, following a real miss — a real correction fixed beats 13-15's attack-grammar language but left "the line of scorched grass" untouched in this exact field): this beat is a LATER field that can carry the wish-twist incident forward — it must NEVER reference scorch marks, residue, a seam/rift, or any other attack-grammar vocabulary from that incident, even in passing ("the scorch line," "the residue," etc.) — see wish_twist_and_arrest_requirement.banned_wrong_visual_grammar / _fatelands_ordinary_wish_misalignment_law.json, which applies here too, not only to beats 13-15.

FULL ACCEPTED SCENE — for continuity only (you are replacing ONLY the 3 [NEEDS CORRECTION] fields below; every other beat/field shown here is already final and must not be echoed back):
Beat 1 [ACCEPTED — do not return this one] (narration, image=intro_lirael): Dawn light cut across the clearing in thin blades, catching on the spiralgrass and turning every edge silver. I stood at the center in the Sacrificiant's sash, its linen stiff against my ribs, the mouth-band tied so tightly my jaw ached. This was the first time the rite belonged to me instead of my father, and the weight of that fact settled behind my breastbone like a second pulse. One wrong step here and the offices I had trained for—Dohkar, Chayr, Provast—would close to me before I ever touched them. The assembly watched without sound, their eyes already measuring how much of my father they could still see in the way I held myself.
Beat 2 [ACCEPTED — do not return this one] (narration, image=intro_lirael): The band smelled of old salt and the hemp it had been boiled in. Cold air slipped beneath the sash and found the skin at my waist where the fabric lifted when I breathed. Every witness stood in a ring that felt too close; I could name each face and knew which ones would carry the story of my failure longest. My fingers found the edge of the sash and smoothed it once, a private check that the cloth still lay straight. The fear lived in the space between knowing every word of the rite and having to speak them aloud while they watched.
Beat 3 [ACCEPTED — do not return this one] (narration, image=intro_seren): Seren knelt on the marked stone with her spine straight and her hands folded exactly as the months of rehearsal had taught her. The blue of her shift matched the dawn shadows, and not a single fold looked out of place. She held her composure like a shield she had practiced lifting until the motion became thoughtless. From where I stood I could see the small muscle at her temple that never quite relaxed even when she smiled for an audience. Her stillness made the clearing feel quieter than it was.
Beat 4 [ACCEPTED — do not return this one] (narration, image=intro_seren): Her gaze found mine for half a heartbeat. I gave her the smallest nod I could manage without moving the band, and her shoulders eased by a fraction. The gesture was ours alone, the same one we had used in the practice clearing when the words still felt new. She did not smile; she simply let her breath lengthen once, then returned her eyes to the stone between us. The reassurance passed between us without sound and left the air between our bodies slightly warmer.
Beat 5 [ACCEPTED — do not return this one] (dialogue, image=intro_dohkar): In the name of the offices that govern this rite I call upon you to name the cost you bring to this First Sacrifice. Speak the irrevocable loss that will serve as its true anchor before the weave and every witness gathered here.
Beat 6 [ACCEPTED — do not return this one] (narration, image=intro_dohkar): Seren answered without looking up. “I give the memory of the night my mother sang me to sleep before the fever took her voice.” The words left her mouth clean and practiced, yet the loss they named was particular: the exact timbre of a lullaby that had belonged only to the two of them, now surrendered so the rite could move forward. I felt the shape of that memory leave her as she spoke it; her hands tightened once against her knees and did not loosen again. The cost was real enough that the clearing seemed to hold its breath around the absence she had just declared.
Beat 7 [ACCEPTED — do not return this one] (narration, image=intro_julian): At the outer edge of the gathering Julian stood with his weight balanced on both feet, the way a man does when he has no need to claim space because the space already knows him. The office of Provast sat on him without ornament, the same rank my father had once held and the one I still reached for. He did not shift or speak; he simply watched, and the stillness around him made every other movement in the clearing feel slightly louder by comparison. I registered the line of his shoulders and the fact that he had chosen the place where no one would have to turn to see him.
Beat 8 [ACCEPTED — do not return this one] (narration, image=intro_julian): I looked away before the look could lengthen into something the assembly might notice. The pull to keep watching him was the same one I had felt since the first time he stood in the same room as the rite I was learning; it arrived without invitation and left a small heat at the base of my throat. I forced my attention back to the stone and the girl kneeling on it. The awareness of him remained anyway, a second thread running beneath the words I would have to speak next.

I recognized the gap between the two in the same instant the rite felt it.
